title: Combinatorics & Modular Math
relevance: OA “number of ways mod 10^9+7” is ubiquitous; stars-and-bars / nCr / expectation appear in Google/Meta/quant screens; CRT/φ are the rating climb
company_notes: FAANG OA staple for ways/passwords/paths/teams mod 10^9+7 via precomputed nCr or multinomial; stars-and-bars as distribute identical items or nondecreasing arrays; expected-value via linearity or E[max] (quant shops); Catalan for valid brackets / binary trees under mod.

phases.goal: Candidate spots modular counting / expectation / CRT signal words and maps the ask to the right combinatorial object.

must_hit.point: Constraints force answers modulo a prime (10^9+7 / 998244353), so division becomes multiply-by-modular-inverse
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names a common prime MOD and says you cannot divide under mod—use an inverse instead

must_hit.point: Signal words include “ways modulo”, “expected value”, “coprime / remainder system”, “valid brackets / noncrossing”, “distribute identical items”
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists several of these phrases and ties them to combo/modular patterns

must_hit.point: Recurring move is rewrite the count as binomial / multinomial / stars-and-bars / Catalan / derangement
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the combinatorial closed form before talking implementation

probes: What phrases or constraints make you reach for modular combinatorics rather than plain DP or search?

hints.1: Look at the output requirement and the nouns in the statement (ways, expected, brackets, identical items).
hints.2: If the answer is a count under a prime MOD, or an expectation, or a remainder system, you are in this family.
hints.3: Say: MOD is prime so invert via Fermat; rewrite as nCr / stars-and-bars / Catalan / derangement / IE / CRT as the wording suggests.

phases.goal: Candidate chooses the right identity (inverse, nCr precompute, stars-and-bars, Catalan, derangement, IE, expectation) before coding.

must_hit.point: Under prime MOD, a^{-1} ≡ a^{MOD-2} (mod MOD) via binary exponentiation (Fermat)
must_hit.evidence_hint: States Fermat inverse as pow(a, MOD-2) and never “divides” under mod

must_hit.point: Stars-and-bars: x_i≥0 → C(n+k-1, k-1); x_i≥1 → C(n-1, k-1); nondecreasing sequences map to this
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives both empty-allowed and positive variants and mentions the nondecreasing reduction

must_hit.point: Expectation: linearity E[Σ X_i]=Σ E[X_i] (indicators), E[max] via CDF, else DP on remaining state
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates closed-form linearity / E[max] from probability DP when the process needs state

must_hit.point: Inclusion-exclusion for unions; CRT when several moduli / remainder systems must be satisfied
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions IE for overcounted unions and CRT/LCM for multi-modulus knowledge

probes: How do you turn “number of ways mod p” or “distribute identical items” into a formula you can evaluate quickly?

hints.1: Ask whether items are identical/distinct and whether empty bins or order constraints appear.
hints.2: Prime MOD → Fermat inverse; identical-into-bins → stars-and-bars; brackets/noncrossing → Catalan; no fixed points → derangements.
hints.3: Outline: identify the combinatorial object, take inverses under prime MOD, and use IE/CRT/expectation only when the statement forces unions, moduli, or averages.

phases.goal: Candidate can state the fact/invFact template and the standard closed forms used under mod.

must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the forward fact and backward invFact build then O(1) nCr multiply

must_hit.point: Multinomial / multiset permutations: n! / ∏ c_i! with inverse factorials
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says multiply fact[n] by invFact of each count, matching Creating Strings II style

must_hit.point: Catalan: C_n = 1/(n+1) · C(2n, n) = C(2n, n) − C(2n, n−1), taken mod p via inverses
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes a Catalan formula and notes the 1/(n+1) is a modular inverse
Gives IE sum or the (n−1) recurrence for !n

probes: Walk through how you precompute binomial coefficients modulo a prime and how Catalan or derangements plug into that.

hints.1: You need factorials and inverse factorials, not repeated per-query Fermat on every denominator.
hints.2: Build fact up to N, one inverse for fact[N], then back-propagate invFact; nCr is three multiplies.
hints.3: State the fact/invFact recurrence exactly, then Catalan as inv(n+1)·C(2n,n) and derangements via IE or the (n−1) DP.

phases.goal: Candidate states the standard precompute/query costs and when IE bitmasks stay feasible.

must_hit.point: Answer binomial-style queries in O(1) after O(N) fact + invFact precompute
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says linear precompute once, then constant-time C(n,k) / multinomial pieces

must_hit.point: Inclusion-exclusion bitmask over k≤20 sets when n is huge
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties subset enumeration to small k (≤20) while n stays large

probes: What are the time costs of the nCr template, and when is inclusion-exclusion over primes/sets affordable?

hints.1: Separate one-time setup from per-query work.
hints.2: Fact/invFact is linear in the max N; each binomial after that is constant multiplies.
hints.3: Say O(N) precompute then O(1) nCr; IE over k≤20 subsets when counting with a huge n.

phases.goal: Candidate avoids illegal division, tower-edge cases, stars-and-bars off-by-variant, and CRT misuse.

must_hit.point: Never “divide” under mod—always multiply by a modular inverse
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly rejects a/b mod p in integers and substitutes a·b^{-1}

must_hit.point: Fermat/Euler towers: a^b mod p = a^{b mod (p−1)} mod p when gcd(a,p)=1; handle a≡0 and 0^0 carefully
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions φ(p)=p−1 reduction and calls out zero / 0^0 edge cases (Exponentiation II)

must_hit.point: CRT: coprime moduli → unique solution mod product; non-coprime ⇒ consistency on gcd; LCM of moduli is the information you know
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes coprime unique CRT from gcd-consistency and LCM as known modulus

probes: Where do people usually break modular towers, stars-and-bars bounds, or CRT on non-coprime moduli?

hints.1: Think about division, zero bases, empty vs nonempty bins, and whether moduli share factors.
hints.2: Towers need exponent mod φ(MOD) only when invertible; stars-and-bars formula changes for x_i≥0 vs ≥1.
hints.3: Never divide under mod; reduce towers with care for a≡0/0^0; non-coprime CRT needs gcd consistency; known residues determine x mod LCM.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use linearity of indicators or E[max] via CDF when the random variable decomposes cleanly; switch to DP on remaining counts/state when the process is draw-without-replacement or multi-type extinction (escalator / bag-of-mice / RPS island).
Prefer C_n under mod via nCr and inv(n+1) when asked for valid brackets / size-n trees directly; some game/path counts are Catalan-like but arrive as DP that equals Catalan—recognize either route.
IE !n = n! Σ (−1)^i/i! is the closed story; DP !n=(n−1)(!(n−1)+!(n−2)) is stabler for modular computation and partial derangement sums with C(n,i)·!i.

gotchas.trap: Writing a/b under a prime modulus as integer division
gotchas.correction: Replace division by multiply with Fermat inverse a^{MOD-2}, typically via precomputed invFact for nCr.

gotchas.trap: Reducing a^{b^c} mod p with exponent mod (p−1) without checking invertibility / zero
gotchas.correction: Use a^{b^c mod (p−1)} only when gcd(a,p)=1; handle a≡0 and 0^0 as in Exponentiation II.

gotchas.trap: Using the same stars-and-bars formula for allowing empties and forbidding empties
gotchas.correction: x_i≥0 → C(n+k−1, k−1); x_i≥1 → C(n−1, k−1); nondecreasing arrays reduce to the ≥0 case after a change of variables.

gotchas.trap: Assuming CRT always gives a unique solution when moduli are not coprime
gotchas.correction: Non-coprime system needs consistency on gcd; the modulus you learn is governed by LCM of the c_i (prime-power wise), not always the product.
